title.narrative: Access to Finance for Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Access to Finance for Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (MSMEs) Project for Cabo Verde is to increase access to finance to MSMEs. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Partial Credit Guarantee Fund to Enhance MSME Finance, aims to finance activities to support the establishment and operationalization of a PCG fund to improve access to finance for MSMEs. 2) The second component, Technical Assistance for MSMEs, aims to finance activities to support MSMEs in generating and providing information to financial institutions supporting their loan applications, including the provision of accounting and auditing services and support for preparation of business plans and feasibility studies for new ventures. 3) The third component, Improve Credit Information Systems, aims to support an upgrade and expansion of the coverage and depth of information contained in the central bank's credit registry, in line with the General Principles for Credit Reporting. 4) The fourth component, Project Implementation Support, aims to cover the project implementation costs.
The objective of the Project is to maintain and increase access to finance to MSMEs in the context of the COVID-19 economic shock.

condition.narrative: The PFIs and Pró-Capital shall prepare, consult and disclose the project's ESMS within three (3) months after the EffectivenessDate and before the beginning of the operations of each of the PFIs and Pró-Capital. This will be an eligibility criterion forparticipation as a PFI and to receive Pró-Capital proceeds.

The Recipient shall ensure that after the Closing Date, the PCG Fund uses the proceeds of any Subsidiary Financing, which areremaining after any payments under said partial credit guarantees, for purposes of providing partial credit guarantees to covercredits extended by eligible PFIs to eligible MSMEs to finance eligible activities to be carried out by said MSMEs.

The Recipient shall ensure that during Project implementation, the PCG Fund uses the proceeds of the Subsidiary Financing forpurposes of providing partial credit guarantees to cover credits extended by eligible PFIs to eligible MSMEs to finance eligibleactivities to be carried out by said MSMEs, all in accordance with the PIM and Operational Guidelines

The Recipient shall no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by theAssociation:(a) ensure that Pró-Capital has opened a bank account to receive Project proceeds, in form and substance satisfactoryto the Association; (b) customize UGPE and Pró-Capital accounting software, in form and substance satisfactory to theAssociation;(c) include Project activities in the scope of Pró-Capital's internal auditor and submit to the Association a reporton a semester basis, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association;(d) prepare an addendum to the Original Project'sexternal auditor contract to include Project activities implemented by Pró-Capital, in form and substance satisfactory to theAssociation; and(e) submit Pró-Capital's audit report for the Association's review, along with the Project's audit report, in formand substance satisfactory to the Association.

The Recipient shall, no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by the Association: (a)update and furnish to the Association for review, a PIM setting out detailed guidelines, methods and procedures for theimplementation of the Project, including: (i) administration and coordination; (ii) budget and budgetary control; (iii)disbursement procedures and banking arrangements; (iv) financial, procurement and accounting procedures; (v) internal controlprocedures; (vi) accounting system and transaction records; (vii) reporting requirements; (viii) audit arrangements; (ix)corruption and fraud mitigation measures; (x) and such other arrangements and procedures as shall be required for the effectiveimplementation of the Project; (b) adopt such PIM as shall have been approved by the Association and shall cause the Project to becarried out in accordance with the requirements set forth in the PIM; and (c) not assign, amend, abrogate or waive any provision ofthe PIM without prior approval of the Association.

The Recipient shall, not later than three (3) months from the Effective Date, appoint an independent external auditor, withqualifications, experience and under terms of reference acceptable to the Association.

title.narrative: Number of approved guarantees for micro, small and medium enterprises

comment.narrative:
<p>According to Pro-Garante, <strong>2.167</strong> guarantees for MSEs have been approved, 367 more than the established target, of which <strong>70%</strong> are MSEs affected by the COVID 19 crisis, <strong>46%</strong> are women-led enterprises and <strong>74.67% </strong>are micro and small enterprises.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: Number of businesses supported with technical assistance

comment.narrative: <p>Up to project closure it was possible to support about 488 MSMEs (exceeding the RF target of 250, of which 199 comprised female led enterprises of, exceeding the RF target of 50), equivalent to a total matching grant disbursement/commitment of US$956k by project closure.</p>

title.narrative: Amount of credit to MSMEs guaranteed

comment.narrative: <p>According to information provided by PROGARANTE <strong>US$ 50,305,131</strong> have been guaranteed to MSMEs, exceeding the established target by more than US$15 million.</p>

title.narrative: First-time MSMEs borrowers covered by the guarantee scheme

comment.narrative: <p>According to information provided by PROGARANTE, <strong>632</strong> MSMEs borrowers had been covered by the guarantee scheme for the first time, exceeding the established target by 382 (of which <strong>375</strong> (exceeding the established target by 300) are female-led enterprises).</p>

title.narrative: Number of signed PCG framework agreements with financial institutions

comment.narrative: <p>[As of end-June 2023, Pró-Garante had guarantees issued with 8 financial institutions (7 comercial banks and one insurance company) - BAI Cabo Verde; BCA; BCN, BI, CECV, FAMI-Picos, Garantia Seguros (insurance company), iiB (international investment bank), and Ecobank.</p>

title.narrative: Businesses satisfied with the technical assistance received under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Data provided by the satisfaction survey among business owners and promoters benefiting from technical assistance under the Pró Crédito Programme on May 2023, carried out by <em>Afrosondagem - Consultancy firm hired by UGPE, </em>showed that <strong>82%</strong> of respondents were <strong>Satisfied</strong> with the services provided, of which, <strong>82% </strong>were<strong> </strong>female-led enterprises.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of adult individuals covered by the credit registry

comment.narrative: <p>According to the Bank of Cape Verde (BCV) Credit Risk Database, <strong>35%</strong> of adult individuals were covered by the credit registry by completion date.</p>

title.narrative: Number of firms covered by the credit registry

comment.narrative: <p>According to the Bank of Cape Verde (BCV) Credit Risk Database, until the month of April 2023, <strong>8.316</strong> firms were covered by the credit registry, 4.316 more than the established target.</p>
<p>Indicator Dropped due to the discontinuation of the Doing Business Report. </p>

title.narrative: Positive financial net results by the PCG management entity (Pr-Garante)

comment.narrative: <p>Pró-Garante’s financial situation has evolved in a satisfactory manner, benefiting from positive cash flow since inception on the back of financial income (interest on the guarantee capital) as well as increasing commission fees from guarantees issued. The audited reports and accounts for 2019, 2020 and 2021 note a positive result of US$10k, US$150k, and US$310k, respectively. The ratio of recurrent revenues to recurrent expenses has been consistently above 1.2, denoting strong operational sustainability.he 2022 audited accounts had not yet, at the time of this report, been officially approved in the shareholders’ general assembly, but do confirm the positive net result trend. It is important to note that project-funding did contribute towards supporting recurrent expenses at inception, namely management and staff salaries as well as office lease, but all these line items have since transitioned to Pró-Garante with no issues. </p>

title.narrative: Percentage of beneficiaries that feel project activities reflected their needs (Citizen Engagement Indicator)

comment.narrative: <p>Data provided by the satisfaction survey among business owners and promoters benefiting from technical assistance under the Pró Crédito Programme on May 2023, carried out by Afrosondagem - Consultancy firm hired by UGPE, applying the estimation of the User Satisfaction Model, with data from surveys to beneficiaries of technical assistance from Pró-Empresa and the credit guarantee from Pró-Garante showed that <strong>72%</strong> of beneficiaries of Pró-Empresa felt that project activities reflected their needs, against <strong>74%</strong> of beneficiaries of Pró-Garante. An average of <strong>73%, </strong>which with a margin of error of 3%, can vary from 71 to 76%.</p>

title.narrative: Mobilization of additional resources from a third party to support co-investments in SMEs by Pr-Capital/Pr-Impacto

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved, considering the US$ 1.5 Million mobilized with the West African Trade and Investment Hub of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) for co-investment in activities that mitigate the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.</p>

title.narrative: Number of co-investments in local firms in accordance with the approved financial, environmental and sustainability criteria

comment.narrative: <p>Whilst Pró-Impacto did not make investments in time for June 2023, it did do so in December 2023, with further investments expected during February-April 2024. The additional financing resources and technical assistance supported directly to Pró-Capital – the development of the Pró-Capital strategic plan was undertaken by a project-funded senior consultant, and was concluded in June 2023, with positive feedback – provided a contribution towards reinforcing its corporate governance instruments and pipeline assessment in line with international best practices. In addition, the capital reinforcement, though eventually transferred to Pró-Impacto, enabled Pró-Capital to effect to raise its statutory investment limits and concluded, as of June 2023, two direct investments in a fishery value-chain company in São Nicolau and a bottling company in Santiago for about US$220k each (Pró-Capital’s ticket size is smaller than Pró-Impacto which operates between US$350k to US$550k). <strong>As a result, only three out of the five end target investments were confirmed to have been met by end of calendar year 2023 (two through Pró-Capital and one through Pró-Impacto), though prospects to overcome the RF target are very plausible particularly through Pró-Impactos’ strong pipeline.</strong></p>
